# Review package

The guide (`guide/indexer-hardening.mdx` and `guide/checklist.mdx`) is published only after a stellar-core or platform engineer has reviewed what it says about stellar-core. This folder is what we give the reviewer.

| File | What it is |
| --- | --- |
| `request.md` | The request text, a draft for a maintainer to send; nothing is sent from here |
| `questions.md` | The 11 questions we ask, each naming the claims and rows it bears on |
| `claims.csv` | The claim-to-source map: every claim of `guide/claims.yaml` with its sentence, kind, verification, review status and a link to each cited source line |
| `unverified.md` | What is not established, what the published table holds back, and the lines published on a code reference alone |
| `high-risk.md` | The claims to check first: what the guide says stellar-core does not validate |
| `../VERIFICATION.md` | The authors' verification report: how each claim was checked and what is still open (built from `verification.template.md` by `verification.py`; `code-refs.tsv` records that each cited code line exists at its pinned commit) |
| `build.py`, `request.template.md` | How the generated files are built |

## Recording the review

Each answer changes one claim in `guide/claims.yaml`: `reviewer_status` becomes `confirmed`, `disputed` or `corrected`, and `reviewer_note` records what the reviewer said. A corrected claim changes the guide sentence and its record together. The docs pull request is opened only when no claim is `disputed` and every fact claim is `confirmed` or `corrected`.

## Building

`.venv/bin/python guide/review/build.py` rebuilds the generated files; `--check` (run by `make verify-guide`) fails when one is out of date. The reviewer can also run `make verify-guide`, which checks the field table against the corpus manifest and the guide against its claim map.
